forest_12_001.speaker: narrator
forest_12_001.text: Rong's brother put his office limit on the table before anyone sat. The paper was shorter than his previous letters and less pleasant. He would acknowledge the twenty-copper credit already granted, the corrected seventy-bag promise, and the removal of the northern remedy. He would not accept any further compensation without a defined commercial loss. Long put the current grain position beside it. Pei brought the deputy's checked record. Lin placed lunch near the door, where nobody could mistake it for evidence.

forest_12_002.speaker: narrator
forest_12_002.text: The injured kiln worker's brother attended for the first session with the worker's offered account. He was not there to make the town buyer pay the entire employer claim. He wanted the buyers' delivery-pressure letters available to that hearing, and the worker's missed-shift advance treated accurately. Rong confirmed both. His brother asked whether the account blamed the office for the closed shutter. The representative answered that it blamed the actual people and instructions in their order, not whoever had the most copper.

forest_12_003.speaker: rong_sui
forest_12_003.text: I supplied the letters. I will not withdraw them now because my brother thinks they may cost us something. They show our delivery pressure and our request for speed. They also show the clerk's altered summary, which I relied on without checking the original promptly enough. The employer hearing will decide how that conduct contributed. We can discuss commercial settlement here without purchasing the injured man's silence as one of its terms.

forest_12_004.speaker: narrator
forest_12_004.text: The cash manager said silence had not been requested. Pei pointed to a proposed general-release clause on the second page of his settlement form. He said it was standard. Long's clerk, who had survived a week of refund corrections, made an audible sound that nobody could call polite. The cash manager read the clause again and crossed it out. His face went red. Lin passed him a clean sheet so the correction would not become another illegible accommodation.

forest_12_005.speaker: narrator
forest_12_005.text: The foreman presented his commercial loss claim: handling disputed logs, canceled northern preparation, and the cost of revising promised delivery. Some costs had already been paid by the council's evidence allowance and could not be claimed again as his own expense. Others were work he had ordered before permission. Pei's incomplete guidance had influenced the line, but the marking sheet still said pending. The cash manager looked relieved by each exclusion. Rong asked him to hear the remaining items before looking victorious.

forest_12_006.speaker: narrator
forest_12_006.text: One remaining item was the lost carriage deposit for the first oversized eastern collection. The town clerk had arranged that collection on his false eighty-bag summary rather than the signed seventy-bag agreement. The foreman had paid six copper toward the slot at the clerk's instruction. The booking receipt and letter matched. Rong's brother could not make the foreman responsible for ten bags his own office had invented. He accepted reimbursement of the six copper from the correction fund.

forest_12_007.speaker: narrator
forest_12_007.text: Another item was a meal purchase for a northern preparation crew called before permission. The foreman wanted it reimbursed as a consequence of the official marker confusion. Pei admitted the misleading guidance, but the independent deputy asked why the pending condition on the marking sheet had been disregarded. The foreman said everyone expected approval. The deputy said the formal hearing would decide that disputed causal share. Interim relief already provided would stand; the remaining commercial claim remained open.

forest_12_008.speaker: wen_cai
forest_12_008.text: We can leave that question open. I know the flour was eaten and the preparation meal was eaten. I also know the men were sent to work under an expectation nobody had authority to finish for them. Do not make us choose a single story because you want the claim settled before the soup arrives. The council paid some handling. The office owes the carriage mistake. The foreman may owe the unauthorized work. Those are different hands holding different ends of this rope.

forest_12_009.speaker: narrator
forest_12_009.text: The cash manager looked toward the lunch pot, perhaps realizing that his impatience had acquired a witness. He accepted the six-copper carriage reimbursement and the preserved claim schedule. He then asked whether the independent imported charcoal could reduce the valley's contingency burden. Long had prepared that proposal. The twelve received bags, six for each buyer, could fulfill the customers' delayed six-bag windows now if those customers accepted the earlier imported grade. Their corresponding local requests would then be canceled, preventing duplicate delivery promises.

forest_12_010.speaker: long_qian
forest_12_010.text: The received bags are the agreed grade, checked dry at twelve kilograms. I can offer the six to the named customers today under their existing price, paying the import difference from my business account. If they accept, six bags come off my local request. Rong can make the same offer to his people. The local reserve does not vanish into a second sale. It remains twelve planned bags beyond the revised local commitments, available for actual production loss or later agreed disposition.

forest_12_011.speaker: narrator
forest_12_011.text: Rong agreed to send the offer. His brother asked whether they could charge the import difference to the customers, who would be receiving sooner. Rong said the accepted delivery terms did not allow that unilateral increase. The brother looked annoyed at the expense and then at Long's quiet agreement. Business rivalry made concession easier when neither wanted to be the only man appearing unreasonable. Lin did not trust that motive to last forever. Today it produced an offer the customers could read.

forest_12_012.speaker: narrator
forest_12_012.text: The buyers took a short recess to obtain the local replies and send the town message. Long's six-bag recipients accepted the checked imported fuel that afternoon. Rong's customers would reply by the next ordinary courier. Long canceled the corresponding six local bags in his allocation request only after acceptance, recording the import delivery instead. His local request stood at one hundred forty-four. Rong's remained one hundred fifty pending replies. The local production contingency grew no larger than the exact cancellations supported.

forest_12_013.speaker: narrator
forest_12_013.text: During the recess, Lin ate on the porch with Wen. He asked whether the negotiation was going well. She said the men had crossed out a bad clause, paid one demonstrated loss, and found a way to use fuel already present without selling it twice. Wen said this sounded like praise written by someone who had learned to distrust adjectives. She laughed. He offered her a bean cake before the cook could discover that their lunch had become another discussion of lunch.

forest_12_014.speaker: narrator
forest_12_014.text: Rong's brother joined them reluctantly, carrying his bowl as if the porch might lower his office rank. Wen made room. The cash manager ate two cakes and asked who had made them. Wen said his sister, whose roof had been finished without the northern timber. The manager asked whether she was the woman whose household pledge had been amended. Wen said yes, and she had a name even though none of their forms needed to borrow her future husband. The manager stopped asking for a moment.

forest_12_015.speaker: narrator
forest_12_015.text: Then he asked whether the good door really shut without lifting. Wen said it did. The manager said their town office door dragged at the threshold, and nobody repaired it because the owner insisted a heavy door looked prosperous. Rong, arriving with tea, said he had complained about that door for years. The brothers argued over which year. Lin listened to their small, familiar quarrel and understood how much of the larger argument had been wearing old family clothes.

forest_12_016.speaker: narrator
forest_12_016.text: The afternoon session addressed kitchen fuel maintenance. Long had funded the repaired latches and trial time; keeping the thirty-bag saving required the scheduled ordinary checks and verified dry wood stock. The cook wanted a specific maintenance appointment rather than permission to report another failure someday. Long booked it with the responsible worker before leaving the table. She inspected the date, then asked whether she could go back to the kitchen. The cash manager looked startled that the meeting had contained someone with a more urgent schedule.

forest_12_017.speaker: narrator
forest_12_017.text: The injured worker's representative left with the agreed copies and no release of the wider claim. He thanked Rong for maintaining the correspondence, then asked the cash manager to send any additional relevant instructions before the employer hearing. The manager said he would search the dispatch book. Lin saw Rong's surprise. The younger brother had arrived to contain cost. He was leaving one subject less contained than before because the record required it. His displeasure did not prevent the useful answer.

forest_12_018.speaker: narrator
forest_12_018.text: At the end, the foreman received the six-copper reimbursement separately from his remaining twenty-eight-copper debt. He could use his business funds as he chose, but neither page quietly changed the other. He said he would apply part toward the next due payment after lawful income. Rong confirmed the ordinary schedule. Wen's uncle asked whether that meant another early installment. The foreman said no. He was learning, with visible effort, to make money last rather than make a receipt look heroic.

forest_12_019.speaker: narrator
forest_12_019.text: Pei left the deputy to close the official record and took the empty pot to the kitchen herself. The cook tried to reclaim it halfway, but the old keeper refused. Lin followed with bowls and found Pei humming the embarrassing romantic verse. She had sung it less since handing over the survey key. The cook supplied the missing last line. Pei pretended to be offended by the improvement. For a little while, no one asked her to be a reliable landmark.

forest_12_020.speaker: rong_sui
forest_12_020.text: My brother will leave tomorrow after he has copied the remaining dispatch entries. He is still angry about the cost. I am still angry that he believed a convenient copy before asking the office that supposedly issued it. We have not settled those feelings. We have settled enough actual questions to stop carrying them into every meal. He took the paper boat from my shelf tonight. I think he intends to return it to the child before leaving. I would prefer he keep it.

forest_12_021.speaker: narrator
forest_12_021.text: Outside, snow slid from the grain-house roof with a soft, heavy sigh. The cash manager stood beneath the eaves, safely clear of the falling edge, studying the paper boat. Lin passed him on the way to the lodging. He asked whether the niece would notice if he took it to town. Lin said she had made him a member of its crew. He smiled reluctantly and put it inside his coat. The ninth week had begun with limits and ended its first day with an object nobody needed to price.

forest_12_022.speaker: narrator
forest_12_022.text: The cash manager left the next morning by the checked lower route, carrying his copied records and the paper boat. The niece caught him at the gate to inspect its condition. One corner had bent inside his coat. She accused him of rough navigation. He apologized with an expression Rong had probably not seen since childhood. The girl straightened the corner and let him go. Rong stood beside the road until the cart turned, then returned to the office without another farewell speech.

forest_12_023.speaker: narrator
forest_12_023.text: The town customer replies arrived two days later. All six named bags could be fulfilled from the accepted imported lot under the original price, and the corresponding six local requests were canceled. The imported twelve bags had now met both buyers' delayed windows. Revised local commitments totaled two hundred eighty-eight bags against the conservative three-hundred-bag season plan. Twelve planned local bags remained the contingency. Pei's deputy checked the entries while the keeper kept actual inventory distinct from that forecast.

forest_12_024.speaker: narrator
forest_12_024.text: The new arrangement improved the margin without improving the forest's yield. Rong and Long had paid to bring real fuel from elsewhere, absorbing its added cost. The customers gained warmth; the buyers gained less profit. The council gained a plan that might survive a small loss without urgent cutting. Lin heard these facts at the shared update and felt relief that required no optimistic rounding. Wen said the margin looked suspiciously like a small roof over their promises. She told him not to make his sister's house do every metaphor.

forest_12_025.speaker: narrator
forest_12_025.text: At the kiln, a lawful dispatch brought the foreman's next income. He made his fourth four-copper installment, leaving twenty-four copper. The six-copper reimbursement had helped his cash position but was not counted as a debt payment until money actually reached the creditor. The clerk wrote the receipt. Wen's uncle stayed away from the desk this time. He had chosen to help replace a damaged shelf in his sister's house, where the screws gave him fewer opportunities to supervise somebody else's balance.

forest_12_026.speaker: narrator
forest_12_026.text: The injured kiln worker's employer hearing took place at the lower work office. His representative attended, with the clinic's restrictions and the worker's account. The deputy keeper admitted the shutter had been left closed against snow. The uncle described tying it earlier. The employer had no posted safe method for that changed drying arrangement and had accepted rush work without checking it. The buyers' pressure letters were included. Nobody could turn one admitted act into the whole cause without confronting the remaining chain.

forest_12_027.speaker: narrator
forest_12_027.text: The provisional ruling required continued ordinary medical support and missed-work payments under the employer's accident terms, with review for the worker's longer condition. The proposed light reassignment could proceed only under medical clearance and accepted pay, without surrendering the remaining claim. The town buyer's possible contribution to the commercial loss would be determined separately from the worker's immediate support. The representative came home carrying a page that meant next week's food could be planned without another personal appeal to Rong.

forest_12_028.speaker: narrator
forest_12_028.text: Lin visited the worker later that day. He looked at the support schedule as though it were a difficult piece of machinery finally moving. He wanted to go back to useful work, he said, but not back to proving he could breathe smoke. His brother laughed softly. The keeper had offered a limited clean-store task when cleared. The worker asked whether visitors would stop asking how he felt once he accepted. Lin said some would probably find a new question. He said that sounded bearable.

forest_12_029.speaker: narrator
forest_12_029.text: On the way home, she found Wen sitting beside the finished house with a strip of cloth in his hands. His sister had asked him to make the feast's small hanging decoration. He was excellent at paper Harts and unexpectedly poor at tying a neat cloth loop. The knot looked like a trapped worm. Lin sat beside him and showed the simple loop she used on her bedding. He accused her of hiding domestic expertise behind grand meridian work.

forest_12_030.speaker: wen_cai
forest_12_030.text: The art of bedding loops has saved this marriage. Do you want formal credit? My sister would write it on the invitation and embarrass us both. I had imagined a great feast so she would know I was proud of her. She wanted a roof, a favorite dish, and people who could come without borrowing for gifts. It is humiliating when someone tells you exactly how to love them and the instructions are less impressive than your own invention.

forest_12_031.speaker: narrator
forest_12_031.text: Lin tied the next loop slowly and left him to copy it. She had learned enough from the washing turn not to offer a larger decoration. Inside, the sister argued with her intended husband about where the lamp should hang. He preferred the beam's center; she preferred light over the actual bowls. They settled on the bowls. Wen said they had already begun marriage without the ceremony. Lin said the lamp had apparently received no ceremonial warning either.

forest_12_032.speaker: narrator
forest_12_032.text: The evening watch heard the adult Hart call from beyond the shallow bank. The voice came once, then waited. Shi Lan took the qualified observer and Lin to the marked point, leaving the route empty. The younger Hart stood with its head low, a root braid caught around a fallen reed cluster. It was not trapped, but turning hurt the bad leg. The adult asked whether the human crew could remove the snagging reeds after they moved away.

forest_12_033.speaker: frostroot_hart
forest_12_033.text: I will take the small one uphill. Do not follow to help. The braid carries dormant buds and old sensations; tearing it would hurt more than you can see. The reeds bend across the bank where the cart wheel scraped them. If your hands can lift that cluster during our absence, the next crossing will be easier. I am asking for a clear place, not offering a new burden to your copper rooms.

forest_12_034.speaker: narrator
forest_12_034.text: Shi Lan agreed to the limited clearing task after the pair withdrew. The habitat worker confirmed which reeds could be lifted without excavating the water edge. Lin assisted by holding the ordinary rope from stable ground. They removed the loose scraped cluster and left the rooted bank intact. The work was small enough that the whole village did not need another meeting. At the end, the shallow turn looked less tidy than a swept road and more usable for the bodies that crossed it.

forest_12_035.speaker: narrator
forest_12_035.text: The younger Hart returned at dusk with the adult. Its braid passed the cleared edge without catching. Lin watched from the agreed distance and resisted waving as though a successful task entitled her to friendliness. The youngster looked toward the humans once. A pale bud trembled in its antler hollow. The adult thanked Shi Lan by name. The warden looked startled. She had expected an observation for the record, not the ordinary pleasure of being recognized.

forest_12_036.speaker: shi_lan
forest_12_036.text: It remembered my name. I have told people for weeks not to turn the Harts into either saints or pests. Then one of them says my name, and I immediately become easier to flatter than my niece with jam. Do not write that in the operational report. Write that the snag is removed and the crossing worked. I will keep the foolish feeling for myself. It has been a while since a forest task ended with so little argument.

forest_12_037.speaker: narrator
forest_12_037.text: Back in the square, the dealer's former poster was trying to sell ordinary cord. He had taken down the disputed premium notice after the restriction and still resented the lost work. Wen bought a short length for the feast decoration at the posted price. The man asked whether the Hart would attend. Wen said no invitation had been accepted. The poster called it an ungrateful neighbor. Wen replied that most neighbors had more useful things to do than watch him tie bad knots.

forest_12_038.speaker: narrator
forest_12_038.text: A stranger at the cord stall asked when the Harts crossed the shallow bank. Lin recognized the grey cap from the witness descriptions and felt her attention sharpen. Many men wore grey caps. The stranger said he wanted to avoid the route while carrying timber. Wen pointed him to the public watch notice rather than give unposted movement details. The man bought no cord and walked away. Lin reported the actual exchange to Shi Lan, including how little it proved.

forest_12_039.speaker: narrator
forest_12_039.text: The wildlife investigator compared the description with the visiting laborer's lodging record. The cap matched a common type; the red strap on his bundle resembled the witness's account. The investigator asked the watch to report another approach without confronting him alone. The current evidence justified locating and questioning the man, not guessing his identity from clothing. Lin disliked that limit more when the small Hart's painful braid was fresh in her mind. Shi Lan saw the dislike and kept the same instruction.

forest_12_040.speaker: narrator
forest_12_040.text: At the lodging, the niece had dressed the paper Hart in a tiny cloth scarf. Wen said the living animal might not appreciate such fashion. She said the scarf was for the paper one, which had no objections. Lin smiled and helped fasten it without borrowing any meaning from the wildlife inquiry. The child asked whether the scarf could go to the feast. Shi Lan said yes, if it stayed away from the soup. The paper animal had acquired a social life busier than its maker's.

forest_12_041.speaker: narrator
forest_12_041.text: Before bed, Lin practiced a short fourth-stage sequence on the cleared mat. Her return remained steadier when she used the slower pace she had learned in cold weather. She stopped within her usual allowance, recorded the actual result, and rubbed her tired hands. The improvement had no new realm attached. It still pleased her. Wen, passing the door, asked whether bedding loops belonged to the same method. She said they were an advanced family technique and charged one bean cake for further instruction.

forest_12_042.speaker: narrator
forest_12_042.text: The ninth week's last morning brought a sharper wind and a message from the habitat keeper. Neighboring observations suggested another Frostroot group would descend from the higher refuge if the current freeze continued. The estimate was conditional; no new animals had been counted here yet. The shallow corridor might soon carry more than the pair already known. Shi Lan read the notice beside the fire map. Two planned uses of the forest were approaching the same stretch of ground, and neither could be postponed indefinitely without cost.

forest_12_043.speaker: narrator
forest_12_043.text: The marriage meal's preparations occupied the house and half the lane. Wen's sister had refused a grand feast, but a small feast still required bowls, benches, grain, vegetables, lamps, and people willing to stop suggesting additions. Lin was assigned the bowls. She accepted the task with the dignity of a cultivator already defeated by several kinds of household work. Wen carried benches from the shelter after the owner agreed to the loan. Each bench had a return mark so the lane would not keep them forever.

forest_12_044.speaker: narrator
forest_12_044.text: The niece wanted the paper Hart to sit beside the bride. The bride said the creature could occupy the shelf above the bowls if its scarf stayed out of the food. Pei brought a small embroidered cloth from her own chest, offered as a gift rather than a keeper's favor. Wen's sister accepted it warmly. Lin saw Pei's shoulders loosen. The official review had made every public gesture feel suspect to the old woman; a private gift chosen freely could still be ordinary kindness.

forest_12_045.speaker: narrator
forest_12_045.text: Rong bought two jars of the favorite preserved fruit at the market and resisted asking whether they should be entered as a commercial courtesy. Long laughed when he heard the question. He was bringing the reserved feast grain under its already paid terms and a separate modest gift of tea. Neither gift changed the household's credits or work. The cook told them any man who explained his gift for longer than a breath would be assigned peeling duties. Their explanations became admirably brief.

forest_12_046.speaker: wen_cai
forest_12_046.text: I have invited the injured worker and his brother if the clinic says the meal suits his current limits. I have not invited the whole timber office, the entire convoy, or every person who once praised the door. My sister made me repeat those exclusions. I am apparently capable of turning pride into a crowd faster than most men can lift a sack. If you see me approach the notice board with an invitation, take away the brush.

forest_12_047.speaker: narrator
forest_12_047.text: Lin took away the brush preemptively. Wen protested until she handed him the cloth loops he still needed to finish. The intended husband came out carrying a crooked stool and asked whether the guest list included anybody who could mend it. Pei said the stool had probably attended enough public meetings to know how to stand crooked on purpose. Wen's uncle repaired the loose joint, now cleared for that modest hand work. The stool became respectable against its will.

forest_12_048.speaker: narrator
forest_12_048.text: At the clinic, the cold-injured boy finished another scheduled check before returning home under the assistant's plan. His warmth and general condition were stable, but the foot still needed protected care in his larger soft boot. The family reviewed the actual follow-up dates and warning signs, not a declaration that winter had left no mark. The grandmother kept the arranged stove help and carried wood turn. Lin brought the paper dog with the niece's renewed permission, and the boy gave it a place beside the boot.

forest_12_049.speaker: narrator
forest_12_049.text: The boy asked whether he could attend the marriage meal. The assistant advised a brief visit only if transport, warmth, and sitting space matched his current limits; the family could decide whether the effort was worthwhile. Wen's sister arranged a place near the warm wall and offered a covered cart turn through the clear lane with the ordinary driver. The boy's mother accepted the short visit after checking the plan. Nobody needed him present as proof that the earlier rescue had ended happily.

forest_12_050.speaker: narrator
forest_12_050.text: When the boy's scheduled check finished, the assistant's paid support for that visit ended under its terms. Home care continued through the family's own arrangements and the scheduled follow-up. The grandmother carried the instructions in a covered fold, the same hands that had once clenched the rope now careful with a page. Lin helped move the family's blanket to the cart. The boy waved from his wrapped seat. She waved back, relieved enough to feel the remaining uncertainty more sharply rather than less.

forest_12_051.speaker: narrator
forest_12_051.text: The upper habitat observer arrived that afternoon to examine the possible migration pressure. He had counted two additional adults and one young Hart beyond the ridge during the latest hard freeze. Their direction suggested descent toward the valley refuge, but the exact route remained uncertain. He spoke to Shi Lan and the local watch, then inspected the narrow bank. The protected turn designed for two bodies would need review if five arrived. The feast's warm preparations had begun sharing the lane with colder arithmetic.

forest_12_052.speaker: shi_lan
forest_12_052.text: We can keep the current pair's arrangement while we prepare for another group. Do not expand the restriction before we know where the newcomers are. I want the upper observer's next report, a survey of the wider bank, and the gathering households' immediate work times. If we need a larger movement window, people must hear why and how their wood still reaches home. A protected corridor becomes a failed promise if everyone outside it is left guessing.

forest_12_053.speaker: narrator
forest_12_053.text: Long offered the storehouse's spare covered waiting space for the gathering families during the survey interval. The space was empty only until the next grain receipt, so the loan had a stated end. Pei's deputy added it to the temporary arrangement. The household elder with the chair inspected the entrance and rejected the icy step. Long had grit laid there before the space opened. Lin liked watching the elder improve proposals through the simple technique of intending to use them.

forest_12_054.speaker: narrator
forest_12_054.text: Rong received a new town instruction urging him to reserve extra local output if the upper trial yields exceeded the conservative estimate. He could consider such output only after actual accepted production, existing commitments, and the contingency were checked. He wrote that condition back. His brother's reply was shorter than usual: understood, report the next inventory. The paper boat had not reformed the cash manager. Seeing the road and the keeper's sacks had apparently given his objections more useful shapes.

forest_12_055.speaker: narrator
forest_12_055.text: The foreman asked whether the four withheld prospective trees might return to the proposal if the migration group turned elsewhere. Shi Lan said their soil-holding role and the land dispute remained regardless of animal timing. The foreman looked bitter. Wen said nothing until they were outside, then asked whether lawful output ever received good news. Lin pointed toward the accepted bags loading at the kiln. He admitted they counted. He had begun measuring good news by whether it removed the hardest problem, which made most good news disappear.

forest_12_056.speaker: narrator
forest_12_056.text: At dusk, Lin and Wen walked the new waiting space together. The gritted step held. The benches fitted without blocking the exit. A child had drawn the paper Hart on the door board, giving it antlers large enough to carry the entire valley. Wen said the real Hart might object to that workload. Lin touched the chalk line and thought of the dormant buds sheltered in crystal. The animal already carried things people barely saw. They did not need to add a town to its head.

forest_12_057.speaker: narrator
forest_12_057.text: The adult Hart spoke from the far bank during the quiet interval. It had heard the upper group's calls at night. Lin stood beside the qualified watch, not close enough to turn the report into an examination. The Hart said the smaller one could keep moving but needed the shallow crossing, and the newcomers might use the ridge turn first. It offered no exact arrival hour. Shi Lan asked the watch to preserve that uncertainty rather than build a schedule from the animal's hope.

forest_12_058.speaker: frostroot_hart
forest_12_058.text: They are not my herd to command. I know one voice and one old scent. When winter pushes bodies downhill, familiar creatures may still frighten one another in a narrow place. Leave an upper opening as well as the bank. If people stand at both ends, we will have space on your map and none in the ground. Tell the hands with the bright flags to look from the path, not only from their table.

forest_12_059.speaker: narrator
forest_12_059.text: The habitat observer checked the upper opening the next morning. One of the manual debris stacks stood closer to it than intended, though still outside the marked bank. The preparation crew moved the loose branches to the approved higher stack, under a paid handling turn already available. The change required no new cutting. Lin helped carry the smaller pieces and found the task easier than her first week. She was pleased until a fork caught her sleeve and reminded her how specific improvement remained.

forest_12_060.speaker: narrator
forest_12_060.text: Wen freed the sleeve and said the branch had evidently not received her progress report. She threatened to make him carry the professionally dressed kettle for the feast. He said the kettle had higher standing than he did and might refuse. The senior worker, passing nearby, said it would attend only if supplied with good tea. The cook shouted from the house that she would put every famous object outside if it delayed the vegetables. The whole lane resumed work with suspicious speed.

forest_12_061.speaker: narrator
forest_12_061.text: The marriage meal began on the next clear evening, early in the tenth week. Snow lay beyond the houses, but the lane was gritted and the door worked. The boy arrived wrapped, with his soft boot supported. The injured kiln worker came briefly with his brother and sat clear of the cooking smoke. Pei sang the full romantic verse before the niece could improve it. Wen's sister listened, then looked at the man beside her with an expression that silenced every joke waiting at the table.

forest_12_062.speaker: narrator
forest_12_062.text: Lin had expected the ceremony to feel like a reward for all the roof work. Instead, it felt startlingly separate from work, a decision two people made while the rest of the valley happened to be watching. The bride spoke plainly. Her husband answered plainly. Neither promised a winter without debt or a house without repair. They promised the ordinary life they were choosing together. Lin, who had spent months examining offered terms, found herself unable to reduce that promise to a useful column.

forest_12_063.speaker: narrator
forest_12_063.text: Wen stood beside the wall with the last cloth loop still in his pocket. When his sister laughed after the first shared bowl, he looked down quickly. Lin gave him time before touching his sleeve. He said the feast was smaller than he had imagined. She said it was full. He nodded, unable to make a joke for once. Above them, the paper Hart watched from its permitted shelf, scarf straight, antlers crooked, finally invited to a room where nobody asked it to carry pain.

forest_12_064.speaker: narrator
forest_12_064.text: The first dishes reached the table while the senior worker tuned a battered string instrument. Its notes sounded as though they had spent years outdoors and had no intention of becoming genteel now. The bride loved it. Wen's uncle joined the song on the wrong beat again, and this time nobody corrected him. The boy fell asleep against his mother after half a bowl, exactly as the short-visit plan allowed. She took him home warmly wrapped before the louder part of the evening.

forest_12_065.speaker: narrator
forest_12_065.text: Rong and Long sat opposite each other, discovering that shared food could contain a rivalry more comfortably than shared timber. Long praised the favorite dish. Rong asked for the recipe and was told it belonged to the cook's memory, which was available only at her convenience. Pei looked delighted by that answer. Lin ate until she was warm all the way through. For a while, the forest beyond the lane was a dark shape whose next demand had not yet arrived.

forest_12_066.speaker: wen_cai
forest_12_066.text: My sister says you may leave the bowls tonight. There are enough hands, and you have been washing since before the roof existed. I am going to dance badly, and I would like one person here who has already seen me fail at knots. It will reduce the shock. You do not have to dance. Stand nearby and look reassuringly unsurprised. If I knock over a bench, you may laugh before checking whether anyone is under it.

forest_12_067.speaker: narrator
forest_12_067.text: Lin danced. The steps were simpler than her practice sequence and somehow harder to remember because Wen kept inventing one when he forgot. She stepped on his boot; he apologized to her foot. The niece demanded a turn between them and improved the rhythm by refusing to be embarrassed. Shi Lan watched from the doorway with the first unguarded smile Lin had seen all week. The promised family evening had survived until the watch bell rang from the upper station.

forest_12_068.speaker: narrator
forest_12_068.text: The bell gave the agreed warning for animals entering the upper approach, not an alarm of fire. Shi Lan rose at once. The accepted relief caregiver took the niece into the warm room while the qualified watch assembled. Lin stopped beside Wen, breathing hard from the dance rather than fear. The feast did not empty into the road. The cook closed the outside door and told the curious children that antlers were not a public entertainment just because a bell had announced them.

forest_12_069.speaker: narrator
forest_12_069.text: At the watch point, the upper observer had counted the expected newcomers: two adults and one young Hart, descending sooner than the next daylight report had anticipated. The known pair stood below them near the shallow bank. Five pale bodies occupied two routes that had previously separated only two. One newcomer swung its antlers toward the familiar adult. The old pair backed down, moving closer to the household approach. The map's upper opening existed, but the animals had not yet chosen to use it.

forest_12_070.speaker: shi_lan
forest_12_070.text: Keep the human waiting point empty. Nobody lights extra torches along the bank. We do not drive five frightened bodies toward one exit by making the other look hostile. The upper observer knows that ridge; he will guide the watch placement. Lin, tell the lower shelter to hold arrivals. Wen, go back to the feast and keep the lane clear with the assigned watchman. The families need an ordinary explanation before curiosity becomes a crowd.

forest_12_071.speaker: narrator
forest_12_071.text: Lin carried the message downhill. At the shelter, two late feast guests wanted to continue through the lane. She directed them to the safe village approach and explained the watch hold. They grumbled about the longer walk, then accepted it after hearing the actual position of the Harts. Lin returned only as far as her assigned point. Above, she could hear a low call and the crack of a reed stem. The two winters had acquired five large bodies arguing over where to stand.

forest_12_072.speaker: narrator
forest_12_072.text: The adult known from the orchard called once to the upper group. Lin could not understand the sound and did not make it into human words for the report. The newcomers moved toward the ridge opening, then stopped. A thin wire line glinted between two stakes where the passage had been checked clear that morning. The upper observer saw it before the young newcomer stepped through. He warned the watch to keep their distance while the animals turned back from the obstruction.

forest_12_073.speaker: narrator
forest_12_073.text: No one could remove the line safely with the group pressed against it. The watch widened the human retreat and opened the alternate bank, accepting that the household approach would remain closed longer. The five Harts shifted in uneasy stages. The known pair moved first; the newcomers followed far enough to clear the stakes. Only then did the qualified observer approach the line. It was a fresh low snare, set across the upper opening after the morning check. Its danger was immediate, regardless of who had placed it.

forest_12_074.speaker: narrator
forest_12_074.text: The observer disarmed and preserved the snare under the wildlife inquiry's procedure. Tracks led away toward the old loading road. One watchman saw a man vanish around the rise with a red strap across his coat. He did not chase alone into the dark. Shi Lan sent the exact sighting and location to the district station. The five Harts remained in the refuge, and the available quiet passage was no longer wide enough to treat their movement as a minor addition to the old schedule.

forest_12_075.speaker: narrator
forest_12_075.text: By the time Lin returned, the feast's music had stopped, but the married couple were still sitting together beneath the dry roof. Wen's sister asked whether anyone was hurt. Lin said no new injury had been found, and the watch was managing the routes. The bride nodded and began sending food to the assigned night workers. The marriage had not been canceled by the forest's interruption. Its first shared act was packing bowls for neighbors who would spend the night making room for five dangerous, endangered bodies.
